Richard Ladson · Certified Medicaid Planner · National Medicaid Planning

Hi, my name is Rich, and I help families pay for Alzheimer's care and other forms of dementia without going broke.

Here is the framework I created to describe the process I follow. I call it the Medicaid Planning Roadmap: three phases, nine steps, from the day a family realizes a parent needs care to approved benefits and protected assets. I coordinate it. At most of the steps, part of the work belongs to another professional, and under each step are the BNI members I would refer to.

Fit with the chapter

My classification: Medicaid planning. I am a Certified Medicaid Planner. I also hold an insurance license, which I use for two narrow products: the Medicaid-compliant annuity a plan sometimes calls for, and long-term care insurance. I am not an attorney, I do not sell health coverage, and I do not handle investments.

I have met with Andrea and with Jonathan, the two members whose work sits closest to mine. Both are people I would refer to, not people I compete with: the legal strategies in every plan are hers, and the health coverage questions are his.

Where I am: the business is new. I can't promise a number of referrals yet, and I won't. What I can promise is the attendance, the one-to-ones and the referrals I've already named, and that every family I work with needs people in this room at most of the nine steps.

The need is not in doubt. Every family with a parent in care faces the same question: how do we pay for this without losing everything we have?

A good referral for me

An adult child whose parent has just gone into the hospital or rehab, or whose parent is already in care and paying for it out of pocket.

You'll hear it as one of these:

  • "Mom's in rehab and they're talking about discharge. We don't know where she goes next."
  • "Medicare is going to stop paying soon."
  • "We're paying for Dad's care ourselves and it's going fast."
  • "Do we have to spend everything before Medicaid helps?"
  • "Someone said we should talk to a Medicaid planner."

When you hear one of those, the referral is a name and a phone number. I take it from there, and the family comes back to this room at step after step.

What I'm asking for

A seat in the chapter under the Medicaid planning classification. In return: I'm here every week, I do the one-to-ones, I bring visitors, and I send the referrals on this page.
